page: UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-8xCPU-32GB is a Cloud Native family virtual server running on the KVM hypervisor. It features 8 shared x86_64 vCPUs powered by an AMD EPYC 7542 processor running at 2.0 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 32.0 GB of system memory, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core. This instance does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, but it comes with one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark results indicate a mixed performance profile. The server demonstrates strong single-core capabilities in specific workloads, achieving a top-tier Geekbench single-core score of 2352.0 and high text processing performance. However, stress-ng single-core CPU performance is positioned in the bottom 10% with a score of 788.49. Multi-core performance across Geekbench and stress-ng tests falls within the average range. Memory bandwidth tests show average read speeds of 54.61 GB/sec for large blocks, though large block write bandwidth is weaker at 25.08 GB/sec.

Given the shared CPU allocation and lack of bundled local storage, this server offers a resource-dense option for workloads that require moderate memory capacity without continuous maximum CPU utilization. It is suitable for general-purpose applications, text processing, and redis-based caching, where its average database operation speeds and multi-core capabilities can be leveraged. It is less suited for high-throughput static web serving or intensive large-model LLM inference due to weaker performance in those specific benchmarks.
